title: Automated intake pipeline and SLA estimator for console analytics asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an automated intake pipeline that classifies incoming console/reporting requests, produces an initial SLA/effort estimate, and routes items to the appropriate delivery lane (self-serve, standard, concierge). The system should reduce manual Triage time by ~60% and give predictable delivery windows for enterprise customers.
context: We receive a high volume of ad-hoc analytics and export asks via support, CSMs, and the feature request form. Current routing and estimates are manual, inconsistent across PMs, and cause SLA slippage for enterprise tenants. Recent incidents: 2025-11 invoice export backlog and 2026-01 delayed dashboard deliveries highlighted the need for a repeatable intake process.
proposal: Build a three-part solution: (1) a standardized intake form with required evidence fields and automated validations, (2) a lightweight classification model + rule engine that maps requests to priority buckets and delivery lanes, and (3) an SLA/effort estimator that returns best/likely/worst case timelines and suggested routing. Integrate the pipeline into Console request UI and the internal Request Queue in Linear via webhooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New intake form deployed behind feature flag; required fields validate and reject incomplete submissions. 2) At least 70% of incoming requests are auto-classified into one of three lanes with confidence metadata. 3) Estimator provides a predicted delivery window (best/likely/worst) for each request; historical accuracy (median error) < 3 business days after 30-day rollup. 4) Auto-routing to appropriate workspace/team queue and creation of Linear ticket with tags and initial estimate. 5) Dashboard shows daily intake volume, auto-classification rate, and mean estimator error.
tasks: - Design intake schema and evidence checklist (PM + UX). - Build intake UI form and validations in Console (FE). - Implement webhook to send submissions to classifier service (BE). - Prototype simple rule-based classifier; iterate with ML team for a light model. - Implement SLA estimator using historical delivery metadata and heuristics. - Integrate auto-ticket creation in Linear with mapping to PM lanes. - Instrument observability (metrics + audit logs) and expose in Console ops dashboard. - Run a 2-week shadow trial comparing auto estimates to human triage before enabling auto-routing.
decisions: - Minimum viable classifier will be rules-first (keywords + tenant size + feature flags) and upgraded later to a supervised model. - Three delivery lanes chosen: Self-serve (ETA 0-5 biz days), Standard (6-20 biz days), Concierge (custom SLA). - Estimator will use a hybrid approach: historical median + multiplier based on complexity signals (export size, joins, custom SQL).
risks: - Over-reliance on early rules could misclassify edge cases for large enterprise exports. - Historical data for estimator may be noisy; need cleaning and explicit labeling of prior tickets. - Users might game required fields to get faster SLAs; require CSM verification step for high-risk lanes. - Integration complexity with Linear API rate limits.
metrics: - Triage time reduced (manual) by target 60% within 8 weeks. - Auto-classification coverage >= 70%. - Median estimator error < 3 business days after 30 days of data. - Number of misroutes to Concierge lane < 5% of routed items. - CSAT for intake experience >= 4.0/5 for pilot customers.

updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting; agreed on three lanes and evidence fields. 2026-02-18: FE prototype of intake form ready; design review flagged missing tenant-usage field. 2026-02-24: BE implemented webhook endpoint and initial rule engine; first 200 shadow submissions processed. 2026-03-01: ML agreed to run supervised classifier experiment; labeled 400 past tickets for model training. 2026-03-02: Shadow trial metrics: auto-classification coverage 63%, median estimator error 5 business days (pilot) — dataset cleanup required. Next: tune rules, add tenant size signal, and schedule stakeholder demo 2026-03-09.
notes: - Include explicit evidence requirements for exports: sample rows, estimated cardinality, destination format, sensitivity label. - For enterprise tenants, auto-routed Concierge requests must include CSM confirmation within 24 hours. - Prepare runbook for rollback if auto-routing causes SLA violations.
customer_feedback: - CSMs asked for immediate visibility into where requests are in queue and ability to escalate. - Two pilot customers requested CSV-only mass exports and asked for ETA guarantees. - Support reported 18% of prior requests lacked clear business justification; intake form will enforce this field.
